questions.topic: eGurukul · Introduction to Immune System Innate & Adaptive Immunity
questions.stem: All of the following are features of immunity given by MALT except-
questions.solutionHtml:
Very specific to the antigen
  • MALT is not specific to antigens as it is a part of innate immunity.
  • MALT. Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue initiates immune responses to specific antigens encountered along all mucosal surfaces.
    MALT is a part of innate immunity. Innate immunity (also called natural, or native, immunity) refers to intrinsic mechanisms that are poised to react immediately, and thus constitute the first line of defense.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 190, 191

questions.topic: eGurukul · Introduction to Immune System Innate & Adaptive Immunity
questions.stem: The lag phase is seen in-
questions.solutionHtml:
Adaptive immunity
  • The lag phase is the period required for the activation of the immune system. As innate immunity is present since birth and active always, thus it does not require the lag phase but adaptive immunity is active only post-exposure to antigen, so it has a longer lag phase.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 190,191

questions.topic: eGurukul · Introduction to Immune System Innate & Adaptive Immunity
questions.stem: Humoral immunity is a part of-
questions.solutionHtml:
Adaptive immunity

There are two types of adaptive immunity:

  • Humoral immunity, which protects against extracellular microbes and their toxins
  • Cell-mediated (or cellular) immunity, is responsible for defense against intracellular microbes and cancers.
  • Humoral immunity is mediated by B (bone marrow-derived) lymphocytes and their secreted products, antibodies (also called immunoglobulins, Ig)
  • Cellular immunity is mediated by T (thymus-derived) lymphocytes.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 190-193

questions.topic: eGurukul · Introduction to Immune System Innate & Adaptive Immunity
questions.stem: Which of the following lymphocytes are found in the maximum number in peripheral blood?
questions.solutionHtml:
T lymphocytes
  • T lymphocytes develop in the thymus from precursors that arise from hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). Mature T cells are found in the blood, where they constitute 60% to 70% of lymphocytes, and in T-cell zones of secondary lymphoid organs.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 190-193

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding Toll-like receptors in humans except?

options.label: A
options.text: It is related to Toll, a gene found in drosophila

options.label: B
options.text: Humans have 10 different types of toll-like receptors

options.label: C
options.text: It inhibits the transcription factor NF-kB

options.label: D
options.text: It stimulates the release of interferon-gamma

questions.answerText: It inhibits the transcription factor NF-kB
questions.solutionHtml:
It inhibits the transcription factor NF-kB

All Toll-Like Receptors (TLRs) signal by a common pathway that culminates in the activation of two sets of transcription factors:

  1. NF-κB, which stimulates the synthesis and secretion of cytokines and the expression of adhesion molecules, both of which are critical for the recruitment and activation of leukocytes.
  2. Interferon regulatory factors (IRFs), which stimulate the production of the antiviral cytokines, type I interferons.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 191

questions.topic: eGurukul · Introduction to Immune System Innate & Adaptive Immunity
questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding Nod-like receptors except-

options.label: A
options.text: Nod-like receptors are located in the nucleus

options.label: C
options.text: Gain of function mutation causes 'Periodic fever syndrome'

options.label: D
options.text: It can be associated with gout

questions.answerText: Nod-like receptors are located in the nucleus
questions.solutionHtml:
Nod-like receptors are located in the nucleus
  • NOD-like receptors (NLRs) are cytosolic receptors named after the founding member NOD-2.
  • They recognize a wide variety of substances, including products released from necrotic or damaged cells (e.g., uric acid and adenosine triphosphate [ATP]), loss of intracellular K+ ions, and some microbial products.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 191-192

questions.stem: The adaptive immune system consists of lymphocytes and their products, including antibodies. Which of the given statements is false?

options.label: B
options.text: Humoral immunity protects against extracellular organisms

options.label: C
options.text: B cells are produced in the bone marrow

options.label: D
options.text: T cells are produced in the thymus

questions.answerText: T cells are produced in the thymus
questions.solutionHtml:
T cells are produced in the thymus
  • T cells are produced in bone marrow but get matured in the thymus while B cells are produced and matured in bone marrow.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 193

questions.topic: eGurukul · Introduction to Immune System Innate & Adaptive Immunity
questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding the activation of lymphocytes on antigen exposure?

options.label: A
options.text: T cells are never required for the activation of B cells

options.label: B
options.text: B cells help in the activation of T cells

options.label: C
options.text: There is T cell-independent activation of B cells

options.label: D
options.text: CD 40 ligand present on B cells bind with CD 40 of T cells

questions.answerText: There is T cell-independent activation of B cells
questions.solutionHtml:
There is T cell-independent activation of B cells
  • Many polysaccharide and lipid antigens cannot be recognized by T cells (because they cannot bind to MHC molecules) but have multiple identical antigenic determinants (epitopes) that can engage many antigen receptor molecules on each B cell and initiate the process of B-cell activation; these responses are said to be T-independent.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 200-203

questions.topic: eGurukul · Introduction to Immune System Innate & Adaptive Immunity
questions.stem: Class switching is stimulated by-
questions.solutionHtml:
CD 40 L of T cell
  • Protein antigens, by CD40L- and cytokine-mediated helper T-cell actions, induce the production of antibodies of different classes, or isotypes (IgG, IgA, IgE), a process called Isotype/ Class switching.
  • Helper T cells also stimulate the production of antibodies with high affinities for the antigen. This process, called Affinity maturation, improves the quality of the humoral immune response.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 201-203

questions.topic: eGurukul · Introduction to Immune System Innate & Adaptive Immunity
questions.stem: Epstein barr virus enters B lymphocytes via-
questions.solutionHtml:
CD21
  • EBV enters B lymphocytes via CD21. Type 2 complement receptor (CR2, or CD21), which recognizes complement products generated during innate immune responses to microbes, and CD40, which receives signals from helper T cells. CR2 or CD21 is also used by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) as a receptor to enter and infect B cells.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 201-203

questions.stem: Which of the T lymphocytes helps in preventing autoimmunity?
questions.solutionHtml:
Regulatory T cell

Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 194-195, 216, 217

questions.solutionHtml:
FOXP3
  • Regulatory T lymphocytes express CD4, CD25, and FOXP3. Regulatory T lymphocytes limit immune responses and prevent reactions against self-antigens.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 194-195, 216, 217

questions.topic: eGurukul · Introduction to Immune System Innate & Adaptive Immunity
questions.stem: Which of the lymphocytes show the phenomenon of Lymphocyte recirculation?
questions.solutionHtml:
T lymphocytes
  • Lymphocytes constantly recirculate between tissues and home to particular sites; naïve lymphocytes traverse the secondary lymphoid organs where immune responses are initiated, and effector lymphocytes migrate to sites of infection and inflammation. This process of lymphocyte recirculation is most important for T cells because naïve T cells have to circulate through the secondary lymphoid organs where antigens are concentrated and effector T cells have to migrate to sites of infection to eliminate microbes.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 197, 198

questions.topic: eGurukul · Introduction to Immune System Innate & Adaptive Immunity
questions.stem: On exposure to an antigen, which mechanism leads to the activation of T cells
questions.solutionHtml:
Dependent on Antigen-presenting cells
  • Antigen-presenting cells (APCs) capture microbes and other antigens, transport them to secondary lymphoid organs, and display them for recognition by lymphocytes.
  • The most efficient APCs are dendritic cells (DCs), which are present in epithelia and most other tissues.
  • Integrins are adhesion molecules that promote the attachment of T-cells to APCs.

Signals: from APC to T cells

  1. MHC presenting Ag to TCR
  2. CD 80/86 activating CD 28
  3. Specific cytokines from APC to T cells



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 196
